findings.summary: NOTE: a guest newListener hook throwing midway through pipe attachment leaves a partial stderr listener and maxListeners=Infinity. The handoff's quoted Astra criterion ('each potentially throwing operation after the first external effect + rollback') usefully identifies this boundary, but F2's established Node baseline is rejected env admission, and traced F2b covers missing/throwing stderr access. Native Worker itself also retains listener/cap effects for this hook fault. Full transactional rollback of arbitrary guest hooks is therefore additional hardening, not a declared Node-baseline violation or missing carrier; the accepted env/option snapshot and stderr-access rows pass.
findings.evidence: Node v24.16.0. Executed `node --import tsx /tmp/pr353-review-stdio.mts`: real io Writable stdout/stderr, stderr.on('newListener', name => { if (name === 'error') throw Error('error listener refused') }), then new WorkerStdio(owner,{stdout:false,stderr:false}); before both [drain,error,close]=[0,0,0], caps 10/10; after throw stdout=[0,0,0], stderr=[1,0,0], caps 10/Infinity (/tmp/pr353-review-stdio.log). Executed `node --import tsx /tmp/pr353-review-native-stdio.mts`: same hook on native process.stderr, new node:worker_threads.Worker('',{eval:true,execArgv:[]}); native stdout listener delta [0,1,1], stderr delta [0,0,0], stderr cap 10→Infinity (/tmp/pr353-review-native-stdio.log). Readable.pipe records its cleanup after dest.on calls (packages/io/src/streams/readable.ts:797); constructor unpipe cannot remove the incomplete registration, and cap restoration is after pipe returns.
